subject: Stochastic tokenflow SLA sim & capacity hedge for StellaGen pilot
messages:
From: Alex Rivera <alex@stellagen.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: megan.cho@stellagen.com, procurements@stellagen.com
Date: Sun, 13 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot throughput & SLA targets (StellaGen)

Hi Karthik —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We want to move the internal pilot to a private/dedicated deployment and need help sizing the capacity before procurement. High-level requirements:

- Expected steady-state: 120 reqs/sec, average prompt + gen ~ 650 tokens per request (mix of short completions and multi-turn chat).
- Peak pattern: 2x sustained spikes during business hours (approx 30–45m) and occasional bursts up to 6x for ~5–10m.
- P95 latency target: <= 400ms for text-generation (model: open-llm-13B quantized).
- Cold-start/cold-KV warming allowed to be slower but should not exceed 1.5s.
- Security: must run in our VPC; procurement prefers a firm-monthly GPU commit for 6 months.

I attached a simple token distribution export (stellagen-sla-sim.csv) and our product team's token-per-turn samples. Can you run a stochastic sim to estimate tokens/sec, recommended commit size, and expected headroom for safety? Also curious how much the KV prefix caching changes GPU needs.

Megan (cc) will own procurement timing.

Regards,
Alex
Director of Platform Engineering
StellaGen
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Alex Rivera <alex@stellagen.com>
Cc: megan.cho@stellagen.com, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 13 Jun 2027 12:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot throughput & SLA targets (StellaGen)

Alex — thanks for the data dump, this is very actionable. I ran a Monte Carlo style sim overnight against your CSV and sketched out a hedging plan. Summary up top, details below.

Quick answer: for the profile you shared (avg 650 tokens/req, steady 120 rps, peaks 6x), we recommend a 6-month committed pool equivalent to 10 H100 GPUs (reserved), with an operational buffer that provides ~35% headroom for sustained peak windows and a short-burst capacity tier (burst-on-demand) that doubles effective TPS for <=10m bursts.

Why 10 H100s? Working assumptions:
- Measured per-GPU sustained throughput (open-llm-13B quantized, optimized kernels, batch-fused): ~20k tokens/sec per H100 under continuous steady-state with prefix KV cache warm.
- With cold KV/warmup penalty, per-GPU effective tokens/sec drops to ~12k (first 2–10 minutes depending on prefix reuse).
- Your steady-state token/sec = 120 reqs/sec * 650 tokens = 78k tokens/sec.
- 78k / 20k = 3.9 -> ~4 GPUs to cover steady-state with warmed KV.
- Accounting for p95 latency headroom (target <=400ms) and variance from request size distribution, plus scheduling inefficiencies, we apply a 2.5x operational buffer -> 4 * 2.5 = 10 GPUs.

KV cache impact: enabling prefix KV caching for common user prefixes increases per-GPU effective throughput by ~1.6x in our sim (reduces token compute by avoiding repeated attention over long context). If you can guarantee >40% repeat prefix reuse during pilot, the recommended committed reserve could drop to 7–8 H100s.

Burst handling: for 5–10m bursts up to 6x steady-state (equivalent peak tokens/sec ~468k), we recommend a mix: reserved 10 GPUs + auto-burst pool (pay-as-you-go) that can add ~14 additional GPUs on-demand for short windows. We also sketch a graceful degradation policy (lower-quality quantized variant fallback) to keep p95 < 750ms if the burst exceeds burst pool.

Latency modeling notes:
- We simulated per-request p95 using a latency model that maps tokens to generation microseconds under typical batching curves. To meet 400ms p95 at 650 tokens, we target efficient batching that limits end-to-end batch delay to <=80ms and keeps GPU generation under 250–300ms.

Next steps:
1) Kimberly — can you validate the per-GPU tokens/sec numbers for open-llm-13B quantized on H100 (our perf lab) and update the sim if measured numbers differ?
2) Alex/Megan — confirm expected prefix-reuse fraction and quiet-hours schedule (this materially affects commit sizing).
3) Laura — I'll need a short ops checklist for private/VPC onboarding and a recommended SLA wording for the procurement doc.

I attached an initial sim CSV and a compute-hedge-diagram.png. I'll follow up with a short note that converts this into a procurement-ready mutual action plan.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: Megan Cho <megan.cho@stellagen.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: Alex Rivera <alex@stellagen.com>, procurements@stellagen.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 10:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot throughput & SLA targets (StellaGen)

Thanks Karthik — quick clarifications from product and procurement:

- Prefix reuse: approx 55% of sessions include at least one repeated prompt pattern (user profile load + standard instruction set). So KV caching should be effective.
- Quiet hours: traffic drops to ~18% of steady-state between 01:00–05:00 local. Peak windows: 11:00–11:45 and 15:30–16:15 local.
- Procurement prefers a commit labelled as "6-month reserved slab" with an option to increase on 30-day notice, and they asked for clear expected monthly token units to justify the spend to finance.

On the tokens: we verified the CSV and there is a heavy long-tail — 12% of requests go above 2k tokens (long multi-turn summaries). We understand this stresses tail latency.

Can you provide an expected monthly token estimate for the recommended 10 H100 commit (with and without KV cache) so we can craft the finance justification? Also please add an explicit fallback latency SLA for the quantized fallback path so procurements can present a conservative risk case.

Megan
Head of Product, StellaGen
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Megan Cho <megan.cho@stellagen.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, procurements@stellagen.com
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot throughput & SLA targets (StellaGen)

Megan / Alex / procurement — attaching the numbers you asked for and the conservative fallback SLA verbiage. Highlights:

1) Monthly token estimates (projected usage profile + 6-month pilot ramp assumptions):
- Steady-state baseline (120 rps * 650 tokens * 24*3600 * 30 days) = ~202M tokens/day -> ~6.06B tokens/month. (Note: that calc uses steady 120 rps; realistic monthly is lower once we apply quiet-hours and weekends.)
- Using your hourly patterns and the CSV stochastic sim, median monthly tokens = ~4.1B; 75th percentile = ~5.8B; 95th percentile = ~8.9B.
- With KV prefix caching (55% reuse assumed) median monthly tokens drop to ~3.0B (roughly 27% reduction in raw compute).

2) Procurement-ready commitment language (short):
"Redwood will provision a dedicated reserve equivalent to 10 H100 GPUs for the duration of a 6-month pilot (SG-4721). Expected monthly tokens under the pilot profile are ~4.1B (median). Redwood will provide a burst-on-demand pool and fallback model variants to maintain continuity under short spikes. Detailed token accounting and usage dashboards will be available in the Redwood Console."

3) Fallback latency SLA (conservative):
- Primary model (open-llm-13B quantized, warmed KV): p95 <= 400ms.
- Fallback model (more aggressive quantization / smaller FFN variant) during extreme sustained overload: p95 <= 750ms, with a best-effort notice and automated rollback if error rates exceed 2.0%.

4) GPU-sizing math (concise):
- Steady tokens/sec required (median sim): ~68k tokens/sec -> requires ~3.4 H100s at 20k tokens/sec/GPU.
- Applied safety multiplier for tail, latency headroom, and orchestration variance: 2.9x -> 3.4 * 2.9 = ~9.86 -> round up to 10 H100s reserved.
- If KV cache effectiveness validated at >=55% reuse, effective tokens/sec/GPU -> 20k * 1.55 ~= 31k, lowering recommended reserved to 7 H100s (we propose a conservative 8 H100s floor if you need an immediate lower-commit option).

5) Ops checklist (short, attached in mutual-action-plan-v2.pdf):
- VPC peering and subnet allocation
- KMS/HSM key exchange and audit logging setup
- Access controls + service accounts for model rollouts
- Canary path and A/B by region for first 2 weeks

Action items:
- Kimberly: please verify lab per-GPU numbers and paste measured values into the shared sim CSV.
- Megan: confirm if procurements want the 10-H100 or an 8-H100 conservative commit for approval routing.
- Alex: if you can provide the busiest-week of the year (if different), we'll re-run the sim with seasonal peaks.

I'll convert this to a single-page procurement appendix and circulate later today.

Best,
Karthik
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
